target.title: policy: classify doctor fix recommendations
target.body:
## Summary

- add policy doctor fix metadata covering every current policy finding
- classify findings as `automatic`, `reviewRequired`, `manual`, `validateOnly`, or `unsupported`
- attach structured `fixRecommendation` data to emitted policy findings without changing `doctor --fix`
- emit `fixRecommendation` through both `policy check --json` and `doctor --lint --json`
- keep policy attestation payloads stable by leaving recommendation metadata out of attested findings / attestation hashes
- add metadata/tests that fail when a policy check id lacks a fix classification

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts src/commands/doctor-lint.test.ts --reporter=dot` passed: 4 files, 329 tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/flows/health-checks.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/fix-metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts extensions/policy/src/cli.ts extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts src/commands/doctor-lint.ts src/commands/doctor-lint.test.ts` passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/flows/health-checks.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/fix-metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts extensions/policy/src/cli.ts extensions/policy/src/cli.test.ts src/commands/doctor-lint.ts src/commands/doctor-lint.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD && git diff --check` passed.

## Stack

Restacked directly onto current `openclaw/openclaw@main` after #99121 merged. Current PR head: `2466c7a3f21afc82848df02ef25886ac0177319b`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Policy doctor findings expose structured `fixRecommendation` metadata in public JSON output for current policy check ids while attestation output remains recommendation-free.

Real environment tested:
WSL Ubuntu root checkout `/root/src/openclaw-workflow/.worktrees/pr-99686` on restacked head `2466c7a3f21afc82848df02ef25886ac0177319b`, with an isolated temp workspace under `/tmp/openclaw-policy-fix-proof.*`. The temp config enabled the source policy plugin, set the default agent workspace to the temp directory, enabled the Telegram channel, and authored a `policy.jsonc` deny rule for provider `telegram`. No live LLM or network provider calls were made.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-policy-fix-proof.*/openclaw.jsonc node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev doctor --lint --json --only policy/channels-denied-provider`
2. `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-policy-fix-proof.*/openclaw.jsonc node --import tsx --eval 'import("./extensions/policy/src/cli.ts").then(async ({policyCheckCommand}) => { process.exitCode = await policyCheckCommand({ cwd: process.env.PROOF_DIR, json: true }); })'`

Evidence after fix:
`doctor --lint --json` exited `1` as expected for the seeded policy violation and emitted this finding:

```json
{
  "checkId": "policy/channels-denied-provider",
  "severity": "error",
  "message": "Channel 'telegram' uses denied provider 'telegram'.",
  "source": "policy",
  "path": "openclaw config",
  "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/channels/telegram",
  "target": "oc://openclaw.config/channels/telegram",
  "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/channels/denyRules/#0",
  "fixHint": "Disable this channel, remove it from config, or update the policy deny rule.",
  "fixRecommendation": {
    "fixClass": "automatic",
    "policyPath": ["channels", "denyRules"],
    "configTargets": ["channels"],
    "summary": "Disable product-managed channels matching the denied provider."
  }
}
```

The supplemental policy check JSON path also exited `1`, emitted the same `fixRecommendation`, and kept the attestation object to hashes/paths only:

```json
{
  "attestation": {
    "policy": { "path": "policy.jsonc", "hash": "sha256:f7bea32f53401bb152a32836107514220ab6282b5f5c7149787f4c5ee3c685bb" },
    "workspace": { "scope": "policy", "hash": "sha256:a03faac8463be7dbad38177af758315a5d39438a2e338118fa1a847adb93ac36" },
    "findingsHash": "sha256:66792d3024b94eeea5769cb13fc07cebad84247704006fa05928741676011936",
    "attestationHash": "sha256:8ba8818628c7e36a6b76e5fa5692fe1ba88923b3530c7ad64c540a42dcea0cf7"
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "checkId": "policy/channels-denied-provider",
      "fixRecommendation": {
        "fixClass": "automatic",
        "policyPath": ["channels", "denyRules"],
        "configTargets": ["channels"],
        "summary": "Disable product-managed channels matching the denied provider."
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Observed result after fix:
Both public JSON paths expose `fixRecommendation` on the policy finding, and the policy attestation remains recommendation-free. The branch is no longer stacked on #99121 in Git history; the PR diff is now 9 files directly against current `main`.

What was not tested:
No packaged release binary, live provider run, or live LLM call was run. The `policy check --json` proof used the source command implementation because this source checkout's top-level `--dev` CLI did not preload the policy plugin command, while `doctor --lint --json` used the actual CLI launcher.
